How does json_tokener_parse_ex read JSON?

Long image

A

Answer

json_tokener_parse_ex is one loop that reads the input one byte at a time and hands each byte to the current state of a 27-state machine. Each nesting level keeps its own state on a stack inside the tokener. So when the input runs out mid-value, the call returns "continue" and the next call resumes at the same place.

  1. Each state handles a byte in one of three ways: consume it (break), look at it again in a new state (goto redo_char), or stop (goto out).1
  2. [ or { opens a container. Each child value is parsed one level deeper and handed back to the parent when it finishes.2
  3. Everything the next call needs is stored in the tokener tok. A few local variables are not, and those cause known bugs when input arrives in pieces.
  4. A final block, out:, decides the error code and, after a success, resets the tokener for the next document.3

Applies tojson-c d2ce61ejson_tokener.c lines 327–1433 (about 1,100 lines)traces measured with a print added at redo_char: in a scratch copy

1

What happens in one call?

Diagram structure
  • Check length, set locale entry
  • Bytes left? peek
  • Run current state dispatch
  • Same byte, new state redo
  • Return object or NULL ret
  • Consume the byte advance
  • Epilogue out: out
  • advance → peek · next byte
  • dispatch → advance · break
  • dispatch → out · goto out
  • dispatch → redo · goto redo_char
  • entry → peek
  • out → ret
  • peek → dispatch · yes
  • peek → out · no
  • redo → dispatch
  1. Check length, set locale ↗

    Rejects len < -1, then switches to the C number locale so 1.5 parses the same everywhere.

  2. Bytes left? ↗

    PEEK_CHAR reads the next byte. At the end of the input it sets "success" if a top-level value is complete, otherwise "continue". With VALIDATE_UTF8 it also checks the byte.

  3. Run current state ↗

    A switch on the current level's state. Strings, comments, numbers and keys use inner loops that read many bytes at once.

  4. Same byte, new state ↗

    goto redo_char re-runs the switch on the same byte, for example when eatws finds a non-space byte and hands it to the saved state.

  5. Consume the byte ↗

    ADVANCE_CHAR moves on one byte. After a NUL byte the loop stops: NUL means end of text.

  6. Epilogue out: ↗

    Sets end-of-input, trailing-character and UTF-8 errors, restores the locale, and resets the levels after a success.

2

What are the 27 states?

GroupStates (json_tokener_state_ prefix dropped)
Flow control (3)eatws, start, finish
Comments (4)comment_start, comment, comment_eol, comment_end
Strings (5)string, string_escape, escape_unicode, escape_unicode_need_escape, escape_unicode_need_u
Literals and numbers (4)null (also NaN), boolean, inf, number
Arrays (4)array, array_add, array_sep, array_after_sep
Objects (7)object_field_start, object_field_start_after_sep, object_field, object_field_end, object_value, object_value_add, object_sep
The switch
25 case bodies: array shares its code with array_after_sep, and object_field_start with object_field_start_after_sep
eatws
A trampoline: skips whitespace and comments, then jumps to the level's saved_state
Literals
true, null and Infinity are matched one byte per visit, counting with tok->st_pos; outside STRICT mode case is ignored
3

How do the states of one level connect?

Diagram structure
  • start start
  • array / array_after_sep array
  • array_add array_add
  • array_sep array_sep
  • finish finish
  • goto out error
  • start → array · [
  • array → array_add · child done
  • array_add → array_sep
  • array_sep → finish · ]
  • array_sep → array · ,
  • array → finish · ] empty
  • array_sep → error · other

Diagram structure
  • field_start field_start
  • field field
  • field_end field_end
  • value value
  • value_add value_add
  • object_sep obj_sep
  • field_start_after_sep after_sep
  • finish finish
  • goto out error
  • field_start → field · quote
  • field → field_end
  • field_end → value · :
  • value → value_add · child done
  • value_add → obj_sep
  • obj_sep → finish · }
  • obj_sep → after_sep · ,
  • after_sep → field · quote
  • field_start → finish · } empty
  • field_end → error · not :

Every level starts in start and ends in finish. A container never parses its own children: array and object_value push a new level, and the child's finish pops back into array_add or object_value_add.4

4

What does a real parse look like?

Measured trace of [1,{"a":true}] passed in one call: 42 state visits on three levels (14 on level 0, 19 on level 1, 9 on level 2). Each row lists the states that saw that byte, with the level number in front.

Byte (offset)States visited, in order
[ (0)L0 eatws → start, which opens an array
1 (1)L0 eatws → array, which pushes L1: eatws → start → number
, (2)L1 eatws → finish, which pops to L0: array_add → eatws → array_sep
{ (3)L0 eatws → array_after_sep, which pushes L1: eatws → start
" (4)L1 eatws → object_field_start
a" (5–6)L1 object_field: the inner loop reads the key up to the closing quote
: (7)L1 eatws → object_field_end
t (8)L1 eatws → object_value, which pushes L2: eatws → start → boolean
rue (9–11)L2 boolean, once per byte
} (12)L2 boolean: the byte after true completes it → eatws → finish, which pops to L1: object_value_add → eatws → object_sep
] (13)L1 eatws → finish, which pops to L0: array_add → eatws → array_sep
NUL (14)L0 eatws → finish, which at depth 0 jumps to out:

A number or literal ends only when the next byte arrives. So [1] needs the ], and a top-level true needs the final NUL or another call.

5

What happens when the input runs out?

Diagram structure
  • Caller app
  • json_tokener_parse_ex tok
  • Tokener fields saved
  • app → tok · parse `{"a":tr` (7 bytes)
  • tok → saved · L0 waits in object_value_add, key "a"
  • tok → saved · L1 in boolean, pb "tr", st_pos 2
  • tok → app · NULL, continue, parse end 7
  • app → tok · parse `ue}` plus NUL
  • saved → tok · resume L1 boolean at "u"
  • tok → app · {"a":true}, success, parse end 3
Kept in the tokener, so it survivesWhat it holds
stack[depth]: state, saved_state, current, obj_field_nameWhere each level is, its partly built container and its key
depth, max_depthCurrent nesting level and the limit (default 32)
pbText of the current string, key, number or literal so far
st_pos, ucs_char, high_surrogatePosition inside a literal or \uXXXX, and the code point being decoded
quote_char, is_doubleWhich quote opened the string; whether the number has . or e
Local only, so lost at returnEffect when input is split
objNone: a finished child is handed to its parent within the same call
nBytes (UTF-8 progress)A multi-byte character split across calls fails with VALIDATE_UTF8 (open PR #1014)
is_exponent, neg_sign_ok, pos_sign_okRebuilt from pb with strchr on every resume: quadratic time (finding 6) and wrong results such as [12 + -3] giving [12] (open PR #1006)
6

What does the out: epilogue decide?

  1. Incomplete UTF-8

    With VALIDATE_UTF8, a pending multi-byte count (nBytes != 0) becomes parse_utf8_string. This is where findings 3 and 3b come from.

  2. Trailing characters

    Stopped on a byte at depth 0 in finish, with STRICT but not ALLOW_TRAILING_CHARS: parse_unexpected.

  3. End of text too early

    Hit the NUL while neither state nor saved_state is finish: parse_eof. It can overwrite an earlier error (finding 5) and miss an open comment (finding 1).

  4. Restore locale

    Puts back the caller's number locale.

  5. Success or failure

    On success, take a reference to current, reset every level from depth down to 0, and return it. Otherwise release obj and return NULL.

7

Where do the known bugs live?

Bug hunt findingWhere in the function
1. [1,2/* returns 2Comment states jump to out:, and the EOF check passes because saved_state is still finish
2. /** x **/ is not closedcomment_end sends a second * back to comment, which then skips the next byte
3, 3b. UTF-8 errors after a valuePEEK_CHAR validates the lookahead byte; out: turns the pending count into an error
4. STRICT accepts {'a':1}object_field_start accepts ' with no STRICT check
5. Memory error reported as EOFThe out: EOF check overwrites json_tokener_error_memory
6. Quadratic chunked numbersnumber rescans all saved digits with strchr on every resume
7. Comments held in memoryComment states append every byte to pb, which nothing reads
8. Locale race between threadsEntry creates c_numeric_locale lazily without a lock

The gate treats fixing any of these as a change in behaviour, so a refactor must keep them.5

8

What must a split into per-state functions keep?

  • state, saved_state, current and obj_field_name are macros for tok->stack[tok->depth], so their meaning changes whenever depth changes.6
  • Each state ends in one of three ways: consume, re-check the same byte, or stop. A state function has to report which one.
  • printbuf_memappend_checked hides a goto out inside a macro, so memory errors leave from deep inside loops.
  • obj, c, str and nBytes are shared by all states within one call and must be passed between the new functions.
  • State the next call needs must stay in tok. The struct in json_tokener.h is fixed, so there is no room for new fields, and a static variable would be shared by every tokener.7
